title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification (abstract page)
note: arXiv abstract page, v1 only (28 Sep 2026), cs.LG, five authors. Compares four probabilistic methods on electricity consumption; says NGBoost has the lowest MAE and RMSE in every zone with high coverage and fairly narrow intervals, ahead of Bayesian regression, MC Dropout and GPR. Names no dataset or horizon. Text licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No code or data link.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting (full text): data and design
note: Tetouan (Morocco) distribution data, three zones, 10-minute SCADA readings for 2017 resampled to hourly. Inputs: hour, day, month and observed temperature, humidity, wind speed and two diffuse-flow variables; no load lags listed. One chronological split, first 80% train, last 20% test. No forecast horizon or issue time: each test hour is predicted from its own features.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting (full text): NGBoost results
note: Table II, test set, kW, zones 1 / 2 / 3. NGBoost MAE 1682.57 / 1400.45 / 1265.71, RMSE 2241.14 / 1799.98 / 1760.22, 95% interval coverage 0.95 / 0.96 / 0.96, mean interval width 8068.97 / 6949.29 / 6601.56. Training takes about 23 s per zone.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting (full text): comparators
note: Table II, zones 1 / 2 / 3. MC Dropout MAE 3014.88 / 2232.26 / 2496.89, coverage 0.92 / 0.86 / 0.77. Bayesian linear regression MAE 3454.93 / 2659.66 / 3410.88, coverage 0.96 / 0.94 / 0.95, widths about twice NGBoost's. GPR fails outright: MAE 32366 / 21052 / 17950, coverage 0.00 and the same width (1239.59) in every zone.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting (full text): what is missing
note: The text gives no code, notebook or data link, no hyperparameters or seeds, no naive or persistence baseline and no pretrained model. It announces a comparison of time-only against time-plus-weather inputs but reports no such table. Test set is one block, the last 20% of 2017 (about 73 days, my arithmetic).

title: Power Consumption of Tetouan City (UCI dataset record)
note: Data record of the series the paper uses (donated 13 Aug 2023; Salam and El Hibaoui, DOI 10.24432/C5B034). Three distribution networks of Tetouan, ten-minute steps, 52,417 instances listed, no missing values. Features: temperature, humidity, wind speed and two diffuse-flow variables; three zone consumption targets. One CSV, CC BY 4.0. The paper cites the 2018 conference paper, not this record.

title: stanfordmlgroup/ngboost (repository of the central method)
note: Repository of the NGBoost library, the paper's best method: a scikit-learn based Python package installed from PyPI, Apache-2.0, in active development (commits in Nov 2026, version 0.6.0 in preparation). It is a learning algorithm trained from scratch, with no pretrained weights, and holds no code for the Tetouan comparison.

title: Research call: code, replication, follow-up (nothing found)
note: One standard research call (LinkedIn excluded) found no author repository, no pre-registration, and no replication or follow-up of the four-model comparison. Its 13 sources: the arXiv record in three forms, the NGBoost paper and repository, the UCI record (two URLs), the dataset's 2018 paper via Semantic Scholar, an LSTM/BLSTM preprint and four tutorials or hobby repositories on the same data.

title: Research source 4: Comparing LSTM and BLSTM Deep Neural Networks for Power Consumption
note: From the research call's source list, not fetched: a 2023 preprint on the same Tetouan data comparing LSTM with bidirectional LSTM. The research answer says it uses different models and evaluation, so it neither supports nor contradicts the NGBoost ranking. Not an independent test of this claim.
